audit.title: Exchange Rate Data Streams

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The implied question ("which exchange rate streams exist and what are their IDs?") is answered by `Loading...`. A lifted chunk contains nothing usable. Weak.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1→H2 hierarchy, 0 level skips — but 0 tables and 0 bullets where a listing page most needs them. Structure exists; content to structure does not.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: 0 numerals, 0 hex identifiers in served prose. For a page whose purpose *is* stream IDs and addresses, this is the core failure.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 internal links (tutorial, discovery endpoint, LINK contracts, supported networks) are relevant and well-placed; 0 external/primary sources. Adequate for a hub page.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No one-sentence definition of "Exchange Rate Data Streams" near first use. Nothing verbatim-liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Valid JSON-LD, canonical, complete OG/Twitter tags — good. Undercut by `datePublished`==`dateModified` (never revised/generator-stamped, and future-dated 2026), auto-generated `keywords` (contains stopword `and`), and template `about` entries ("Content about exchange").

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code; limited applicability for a listing page, but a verification snippet using a real stream ID would help agents.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Title matches "exchange rate data streams," but no symptom/how-to phrasing and no served answers. Devs asking "what is the stream ID for X exchange rate?" get nothing.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: The sparse prose is clean and consistent; there is simply almost none of it.

audit.summary: This is a reference listing page whose entire payload — the table of exchange rate streams, their IDs, and verifier addresses — is client-side rendered and absent from the served HTML (the body reads `Loading...`, 55 words total, 0 tables, 0 numerals). The single biggest strength is clean schema/metadata scaffolding (valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList`, canonical URL). The single biggest opportunity, which dominates everything else, is that **generative engines and agents that don't execute JavaScript see an empty page** — the very data this page exists to provide is invisible to retrieval. This is not a prose-polish problem; the page cannot be cited for facts it never serves.

recommendations.title: Server-render the stream listing so IDs and addresses are in the HTML
recommendations.issue: `Loading...` — the entire dataset is client-side and absent from served markup.
recommendations.change: Pre-render (SSR/SSG) the full stream table into static HTML so non-JS crawlers and agents receive stream names, IDs, feed/verifier addresses, and networks without executing scripts.
recommendations.why: Retrieval is the dominant loss; a page that serves no facts cannot be cited or synthesized regardless of schema quality.

recommendations.title: Emit the stream inventory as a real semantic `<table>`
recommendations.issue: 0 tables, 0 bullets on a listing page.
recommendations.change: Columns: Stream name · Stream ID (hex) · Asset pair · Network · Verifier proxy address · Decimals/format. One row per stream, header row present.
recommendations.why: Comparison tables are high-lift for extraction; engines lift row-scoped facts and answer "what's the ID for X" precisely.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first canonical definition in the first sentence
recommendations.where: Directly under the H1, before the tutorial link
recommendations.issue: Page opens with "To learn how to use Data Streams, see…" — a redirect, not an answer.
recommendations.change: Add a self-contained lead: "Exchange Rate Data Streams provide onchain exchange-rate values for [assets]. Each stream is identified by a 32-byte stream ID and verified via the network's verifier proxy. The available streams and IDs are listed below."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-liftable definition and a chunk that stands alone.

recommendations.title: Fix freshness signals
recommendations.issue: Identical timestamps, future-dated `2026-09-21` — reads as generator-stamped, never revised.
recommendations.change: Emit true last-modified on data changes and surface a visible "Last updated" line on-page.
recommendations.why: Divergent, plausible dates and visible freshness raise E-E-A-T trust for a page that changes as streams are added.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased subheadings
recommendations.issue: Only concept-titled headings ("Streams Verifier Network Addresses").
recommendations.change: Add H2/H3s phrased as queries: "What is the stream ID for [pair]?", "Which networks support exchange rate streams?", "Verifier proxy address by network".
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by task and symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles miss.

recommendations.title: Replace auto-generated schema fields with meaningful values
recommendations.change: Set `about` to real entities (Chainlink Data Streams, exchange rate feeds, verifier proxy) and curate keywords; ideally add `ItemList`/`Dataset` schema describing the stream inventory.
recommendations.why: Template placeholders add no entity signal; a `Dataset`/`ItemList` graph makes the listing machine-parseable.

antiPatterns: **Wall of nothing / unrendered content:** primary content served as `Loading...` — the most severe issue on the page.
**Auto-generated metadata fluff:** template `about` descriptions and a stopword in `keywords`.
**Answer-deferral opener:** page leads with a "see the tutorial" pointer rather than its own answer.
offPageNotes: Consider an `llms.txt` and a machine-readable endpoint (JSON/CSV) for the stream inventory so agents can fetch IDs without scraping rendered tables.
Site-level: ensure the discovery API page and `supported-networks` page link back to this hub (canonical-hub pattern) so authority concentrates here.
The CLI should confirm whether the SSR/hydrated DOM (post-JS) contains the table; this audit reflects the served HTML, which does not.
